title: もの and こと: advanced uses
summary: もの is a noun, a thing, even an abstract one. こと is a fact or state of affairs: したことがある, することがある, and sentence-ending ものだ.

blocks.text: The usual advice says **もの** is concrete (a pencil) and **こと** abstract (a situation). That is a fine start, but it breaks down. What もの really means is **a thing**, a noun: it can be an apple or it can be love. **こと** is a **state of affairs**, a fact, something that happens or exists.

blocks.jp: 愛は素晴らしいものだ。
blocks.en: Love is a wonderful thing. (love is a noun, a thing)

blocks.text: ことがある: the fact exists

Japanese has no separate perfect tense. It says that **the fact of having done it exists**. Put the verb in the **past** and you have experience; put it in the **present** and you have something that sometimes happens.

blocks.jp: 日本に行ったことがある。
blocks.en: I have been to Japan. (the fact of having gone exists)

blocks.jp: 日本に行くことがある。
blocks.en: I sometimes go to Japan. (the fact of going exists)

blocks.jp: 誰でも失敗することがある。

blocks.text: ものだ as a sentence ender

Adding **ものだ** to a full sentence turns it into a **thing**: a reality you have to accept, "that's just how it is". The generalization has to be in the present. In the **past**, **〜たものだ** becomes a personal memory: "I used to...", with feeling.

blocks.en: Winter is cold, that's just how it is.

blocks.jp: 子供のころ、よくここに来たものだ。
blocks.en: As a child I used to come here often.

blocks.text: At the end of a written rule, **こと** works as a firm instruction.

blocks.en: Hand in your homework without fail.

items: **もの**: a thing (any noun, concrete or abstract).
**こと**: a fact or situation. **〜たことがある** = have done; **〜ることがある** = sometimes happens.
**〜ものだ** (present) = that's how it is; **〜たものだ** = used to, with feeling.
Rules and notices can end in **こと**: "do it."

questions.prompt: 日本に行った＿＿がある。 (I have been to Japan.)
questions.note: The fact of having gone exists: ことがある.

questions.prompt: 日本に行くことがある。
options: I will never go to Japan
I want to go to Japan

questions.prompt: 日本に行ったことがある。
options: I used to want to go to Japan
questions.note: Past tense: the fact of having gone exists.

questions.instruction: Why does 愛は素晴らしいものだ use もの?
options: Love is a noun, a thing, even though abstract
Love can be held in your hand
The sentence is in the past
questions.note: もの simply means a thing, and love is a noun.

options: Winter is cold; that is just how it is
I want winter to be cold
questions.note: Present ものだ states a generalization you must accept.

questions.prompt: 子供のころ、よくここに来たものだ。
options: I used to come here often as a child
questions.note: Past ものだ is a feeling-laden memory.

questions.prompt: もの can only refer to objects you can hold in your hand.
questions.note: もの is any noun-thing, including abstract ones like love.

questions.instruction: Which sentence carries the warm, remembering feeling of "I used to"?
options: よくここに来たものだ
ここに来たことがある

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "the fact exists"
What does 宿題は必ず出すこと。 mean on a classroom wall?
options: Hand in your homework without fail
questions.note: こと at the end of a rule is an instruction.

questions.prompt: 誰でも失敗する＿＿がある。 (Everyone fails sometimes.)
questions.note: することがある: sometimes happens.
